text: {"lessons":["Repeatedly taking gains in Stock A and D did not protect my account from later losses; I should focus on the portfolio’s overall return and risk, not the comfort of realized wins.","Selling only because a position is above my average cost can leave me underexposed to future gains. I should base each decision on the stock’s prospects and my target allocation, not my purchase price.","My late sales of A and B at steep losses show the danger of letting losses linger while reacting emotionally. I should review deteriorating holdings promptly and use clear, consistent position and risk limits."]}
